content: The coadministration of certain drugs with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF can result in significant pharmacokinetic interactions due to the inhibition or induction of hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, CYP2D6, and CYP2C9/10, as well as the modulation of renal clearance mechanisms. Below are the detailed interactions and clinical recommendations: 1. Hydrocodone: Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 2. Ibuprofen: Concurrent use with emtricitabine and tenofovir may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and therapy should be closely monitored. 3. Ifosfamide: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Iloperidone: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases iloperidone levels via CYP2D6 inhibition, while iloperidone increases elvitegravir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Imatinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat can both increase and decrease imatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, respectively. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 6. Imipramine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6. Caution is advised with CYP2D6 substrates, and therapy should be closely monitored. 7. Indomethacin: Coadministration with emtricitabine and tenofovir may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 8. Irinotecan: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases elvitegravir/cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are required. 10. Isosorbide Dinitrate and Mononitrate: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases their levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 11. Isradipine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases isradipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 12. Istradefylline: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases istradefylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 13. Itraconazole: Both elvitegravir/cobicistat and itraconazole are CYP3A4 inhibitors. Itraconazole dose should not exceed 200 mg/day when coadministered. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 14. Ivacaftor: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Ivacaftor dose should be reduced when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific product guidelines for dosage adjustments. 15. Ixabepilone: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases ixabepilone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Ketamine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat decreases ketamine levels by inducing CYP2C9/10. Caution and close monitoring are required. 17. Ketoconazole: Both elvitegravir/cobicistat and ketoconazole are CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole dose should not exceed 200 mg/day when coadministered. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 18. Ketoprofen: Coadministration with emtricitabine and tenofovir may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and therapy should be closely monitored. 19. Ketorolac (including intranasal): Coadministration with emtricitabine and tenofovir may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and therapy should be closely monitored. 20. Lacosamide: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases lacosamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose reduction of lacosamide should be considered when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Lapatinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 22. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: These agents increase elvitegravir/cobicistat levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Tenofovir levels may increase, necessitating dose regimen adjustments. 23. Levoketoconazole: Elvitegravir/cobicistat and levoketoconazole are both CYP3A4 inhibitors. Levoketoconazole dose should not exceed 200 mg/day when coadministered. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Levomilnacipran: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases levomilnacipran levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Lidocaine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases lidocaine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Losartan: Elvitegravir/cobicistat can both increase and decrease losartan levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, respectively. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 27. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose adjustments are necessary when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Lumataperone: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases lumataperone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose should be limited to 5 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Magnesium Oxide: Magnesium oxide decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration from antacids by at least 2 hours. 30. Maprotiline: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases maprotiline levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Caution is advised with CYP2D6 substrates, and therapy should be closely monitored. 31. Mavorixafor: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases mavorixafor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein modulation. Monitor mavorixafor levels and reduce the dose if necessary. 32. Meclofenamate: Coadministration with emtricitabine and tenofovir may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and therapy should be closely monitored. 33. Medroxyprogesterone: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases medroxyprogesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 34. Mefenamic Acid: Coadministration with emtricitabine and tenofovir may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and therapy should be closely monitored. 35. Mefloquine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases mefloquine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Each interaction requires careful consideration of the pharmacokinetic mechanisms involved, and therapy should be adjusted accordingly to minimize the risk of adverse effects or toxicity.
